A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Timer-XL research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v3 reports original Timer-XL forecasting results, pre-training generalization experiments, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains original Timer-XL experiments and analyses in the main text and appendices, including forecasting results and attention ablations.

M1.justification: The multivariate next-token objective, decoder-only architecture, Kronecker attention mask, temporal RoPE, variable embeddings, and forecasting procedure remain unchanged. Replacing 'generative' with 'causal' or 'decoder-only' does not establish a method change.

E1.justification: The forecasting datasets, task families, ERA5 generalization scenarios, and UTSD/LOTSA pre-training coverage are retained. LOTSA was already used in v3; its new dataset-table row documents existing coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding full comparisons retain their comparator sets. Time-MoE Base, Large, and Ultra now appear in the main zero-shot summary, but all three already participated in the same benchmark in v3 Table 12, retained as v4 Table 13.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 revises the shorter pre-training context from 672 to 1440, retaining the longer context of 2880. The 27B LOTSA pre-training statement disappears, while v4 Table 9 reports 231,082,956,489 training time points; whether this reflects changed usage or corpus accounting is unexplained. These disclosures do not establish reruns. Four-horizon zero-shot evaluation already existed in v3.

E4.justification: The architecture/channel-dependence comparisons, causal covariate ablation, positional-embedding and normalization ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity curves, and attention case studies are retained. Renaming 'Analysis' to 'Ablation Study' and moving appendix material do not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: v3 Table 9 and v4 Table 10 report identical results and standard deviations from three random seeds. No new repeated-run information, uncertainty procedure, confidence interval, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: The separate UTSD/LOTSA pre-training comparison in v3 Table 6 is dropped, including the LOTSA-only ETTh1 result of 0.363 MSE and 0.390 MAE. Every row of v4 Table 7 instead reproduces an average already reported in v3 Table 12. The full zero-shot and multivariate appendix results remain identical, so this is limited removal and repackaging, not a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The method equations and Appendix A derivations are unchanged. v4 Table 8 separates operation counts from asymptotic complexity and restates counts already derived in v3, rather than introducing a new proof or mathematical result.

C1.justification: v4's abstract explicitly claims state-of-the-art zero-shot performance, whereas v3's abstract says 'notable' and its introduction qualifies outperformance by comparable pre-training scale and model size. This modestly strengthens the headline performance claim; the methodological contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 replaces normalization's sample-enrichment explanation with simplified learning, restricted model capacity, and possible mode collapse. Section 4.2 describes suitability with sufficient training samples instead of arbitrary prediction horizons. The substantive limitations in Appendix F are retained.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-repository pointer in the abstract and documents LOTSA's dataset length and 2880-to-96 training setting in Table 9. The checkpoint link already existed in v3. Hardware, optimizer, and the detailed model-configuration table remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Table 1 explicitly positions Timer-XL against existing Transformers by intra-series modeling, inter-series modeling, causality, and pre-training. v4 adds a PEMS source reference and removes background references to Transformer-XL, ViT, GPT, and language-model scaling laws.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, experimental framing, and conclusion receive substantial rewriting. Terminology systematically shifts toward causal/decoder-only Transformers, and the narrative more directly distinguishes task-specific forecasting, pre-training, and model analysis. This is extensive editorial revision despite stable scientific content.

P2.justification: v4 adds the model-comparison table, restructures the zero-shot summary and complexity table, refines labels in Figures 5, 7, and 12, and rearranges Figure 11 panels and appendix floats. Most plots and table displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The clearer narrative, architectural comparison table, and main zero-shot summary aligned with the retained appendix results make the paper easier to assess. The explicit code pointer improves reproducibility information. These are modest gains: scientific validation is unchanged, separate pre-training-corpus scores are omitted, and the revised LOTSA volume remains unexplained.
